name: Tobi Lawal
notes: A London-raised Virginia Tech senior and the program's first draftee since Nickeil Alexander-Walker in 2019 (12.3/8.5/1.1 blk on 54/25/76% shooting), whose 45.5-inch max vertical and 40.0-inch no-step vertical at the Combine ranked among the best ever recorded. Dallas took him 48th and signed him to a two-way contract; he opened the 2026 Summer League with Dallas. His NBA career begins with the 2026-27 season — no regular-season games played yet.

name: Bryce Hopkins
notes: A two-time All-Big East St. John's forward (13.6/6.2 on 47% shooting), a physical rebounder and slasher, part of the third player from the Red Storm drafted this year alongside Zuby Ejiofor (23rd, Atlanta) and Dillon Mitchell (40th, Boston) — St. John's best draft class in 43 years. Denver took him 49th. His NBA career begins with the 2026-27 season — no regular-season games played yet.

name: Lajae Jones
notes: A well-traveled forward whose final stop was Florida State (12.7/5.7 career), the first player drafted from the program's new Luke Loucks era, an athletic, moldable two-way wing prospect. Golden State took him 54th. He does not appear in the tool's original pre-draft board data. His NBA career begins with the 2026-27 season — no regular-season games played yet.

name: Vsevolod Ishchenko
notes: A Russian guard for PBC Lokomotiv Kuban in the VTB United League (8.7/4.7/2.0/1.3 stl on an elite 51.6/46.3/80.1% shooting, VTB League All-Star and Young Player of the Year), real, proven senior-level European production. Chicago took him 56th, his rights traded to Dallas via the Lakers. He does not appear in the tool's original pre-draft board data. His NBA career begins whenever he signs — no regular-season games played yet.

name: Narcisse Ngoy
notes: A French big man who played in France's second division (solid rebounding and shot-blocking numbers), a real defensive-anchor prospect projecting on lob finishing and screen-and-roll defense. Atlanta took him 57th, immediately trading his rights to the Clippers — but rather than turn pro, Ngoy chose to sign with Auburn for 2026-27, an unusual draft-then-college path believed to be the first of its kind in the modern era. He does not appear in the tool's original pre-draft board data. Never played in the NBA — he'll play college basketball this season instead.
